cards.speaker: James
cards.text: The business needs to be better than it is. We need to be recognised as experts producing quality products.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: I'll be plain. We'll be judged on the work, and the work isn't good enough yet.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Whatever we choose this week, it should leave us ahead of the Guild's standard, not behind it.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Right. What we need is money in the bank, so a bad week stops being a crisis.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Simple question: what gets us more cash and less worry? That's what I'm after.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Rent doesn't care how good our calc is. I want us comfortable first, then we can be proud.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Um. Sorry. I think the business needs to focus on the veins right now. Without them, we can't sell ore, or craft items.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: I don't want to say the wrong thing. I think we need more coming out of the veins, and the rest follows.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Sorry, can I start? I think we should be sure of what we've got first. The veins, I mean.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Money buys us a better bench. I'll give you that, Archie.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: A firm afraid of its bills makes rushed work. You're right about the cash.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Fine. If it stops us worrying about the rent, I can work in peace. I'll back it.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Selling more doesn't make it good. You're counting pounds, I'm counting quality.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Chasing cash alone won't reduce your worries, Archie. Buyers who only want the cheap stuff leave when someone is cheaper.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: You keep saying safe. A business that makes forgettable or sub-par work is never safe.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: More from the veins means more to craft. Sensible, Owen.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Agreed. I can't craft what we haven't got.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: That, at least, I can find no fault with.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: More of the same ore doesn't improve our situation, Owen. Yield without craft simply results in a bigger pile.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Quantity is the easy part, Owen. What would we do with it?

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: That's what you always propose. Why is this week different?

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Better work means we can ask more for it. I like that, James.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: If it's good enough, buyers pay more. Fair enough.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Go on, then, make it better. Just make sure someone's buying it.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Lovely work, James. Does it sell? Rent's due either way.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Being proud of it doesn't pay the bills. Who's buying?

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: It's the Guild this and the Guild that every week. I'm trying to pay for things, not win an argument.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: More from the veins is more to sell. Good call, Owen.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Can't argue with that. More stock, more sales, and nobody has to worry.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: You picked a good one, Owen. I'll back it.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: More stock's no use if it sits there, Owen. Who's selling it?

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Yeah, but more of what? If nobody wants it, it's just more to store.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: I like it, Owen, but I want the plan to include the part where it turns into money.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Sorry, James, that sounds right. Could the veins come into it somehow?

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: I'm not sure I know enough to say. Would it need more from the veins, do you think?

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: That sounds sensible, I think. Though the veins would have to supply it.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Sorry, Archie, that makes sense. Could the veins come into it somehow?

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: I'm not sure I can judge the money. Would it need more from the veins, do you think?

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: That sounds sensible, I think. The veins would have to bring in the stock, though. Sorry.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Buyers pay more for good work, and they come back for it. Improving quality is the right way forward.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: I'll grant it takes longer. It also lasts longer, and so does our name.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: You may be right about the timing. I'm still right about the work.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Fine, but cash is what lets us fix everything else. Bills first, then the nice stuff.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: I hear you. But the bank doesn't take pride, it takes pounds.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Fair point, and I'll watch that. But money's still what keeps the lights on.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Sorry, I know. But it all starts with the veins. If they give more, everything else has more to work with.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: You're right, I didn't think about that. I still think it's worth doing, though. If that's all right.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: I just think it's the safe bit. We know the veins. We don't have to guess.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: You'd sell anything someone would pay for, Archie.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Anything decent, and nobody's complained yet. Pride's lovely, James, but I can't pay the rent with it.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: The Guild wouldn't put its name on a rushed job for the sake of cash.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: The Guild has money behind it. We don't, so I'd like some of that first.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: You think every problem is a shortage of money.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Name one that's easier with less of it.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Owen, more yield is great, but the extra's only worth something if we sell it.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Yes, sorry, you're right. I just thought that with more of it, selling would be easier.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: You pitch the same thing every time, Owen. Veins, veins, veins.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: I know. Sorry. It's what I understand, and I'd rather be right about a small thing than wrong about a big one.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Do you ever want to try a bigger number, Owen?

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Sometimes. Then I think about what happens if I'm wrong, and I'd rather not find out.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Owen, you can't keep proposing more as if more were an answer.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Sorry, James. It's just that I can see more, and I'm not sure I can see better.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Tell me you'd at least like the work to be good.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: I would! I'd just like to be sure there's something to make it from first.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: You know the veins better than any of us. Why do you apologise for it?

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Habit, I think. Sorry. Sorry about saying sorry.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: {label}. Good. Now we do it properly.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: {label}, then. I'll hold us to the standard.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Sensible choice. {label}, and no corners cut.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: {label}. Lovely. That'll help the books.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Good. {label}. Let's start on it today.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: {label}, then. Nice and simple, how I like it.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Oh. {label}? Thank you. I'll do my best.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Really? {label}. Right. I'll get it right, I promise.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: {label}, then. Thanks. Sorry, I mean, thank you.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Very well. Do it properly, though.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Not what I'd have picked. But I'll live.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Acceptable. Don't mistake that for enthusiasm.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Fair enough. Your call. I'll sort the money side.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Not my pick, but fine. We'll see what it brings in.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Go on, then. I'll find a way to make it pay.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Oh, good. I mean, whatever you think is best.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: That's all right. I wasn't sure about mine anyway.

cards.speaker: Owen
cards.text: Sorry, I'll help however I can.
